analysis.investment_thesis: Manorama scores adequately on Return on Capital (~20% ROCE) but fails catastrophically on Earnings Yield — EBIT of INR 186 Cr against an EV of ~INR 8,944 Cr produces just a 2.1% earnings yield, far below my 12% minimum. The Magic Formula requires BOTH metrics to be attractive; here, only one qualifies, and the other is disqualifying.
key_strengths: Growing niche moat in specialty fats/shea butter — operating margins expanded from 13.7% (2022) to 24.1% (2025), signaling pricing power
Revenue CAGR of 40.5% and EBIT CAGR of 69.2% over 3 years — scale is clearly being gained in a specialized ingredient space
ROCE of ~20% and ROE of 23.9% — adequate return on capital meeting Greenblatt's lower threshold
key_risks: Earnings yield of 2.1% (EBIT 186 Cr / EV ~8,944 Cr) — the stock is priced for perfection at 39.5x P/E and 26.5x EV/EBITDA
Chronically negative free cash flow: FCF was negative in 3 of 4 years (-93, +8, -193, -89 Cr) — reported profits are not converting to cash
Finance costs growing at 100% CAGR (5 Cr → 39 Cr) and debt ballooning from 108 Cr to 482 Cr — balance sheet risk rising fast
red_flags: Earnings Yield of 2.1% — deeply below the 6% floor required by the Magic Formula
Operating CF negative in 3 of 4 years: INR 110 Cr net profit in FY25 but OCF of -57 Cr and FCF of -89 Cr suggests aggressive working capital build or accounting-cash disconnect
Cash near zero (INR 3 Cr vs. INR 482 Cr debt) with financing flows the only lifeline — highly dependent on capital markets
analysis.detailed_analysis:
By the Magic Formula, the two questions are: is the business good (ROIC), and is it cheap (Earnings Yield)? Manorama's ROCE of ~20% is borderline acceptable — it clears my 20% threshold just barely, and the expanding operating margins (13.7% in 2022 to ~24% in 2025) suggest some real competitive advantage in specialty fats sourcing. However, the business earns INR 186 Cr in EBIT against an enterprise value of roughly INR 8,944 Cr — that's a 2.1% earnings yield. My framework requires >12% to rank favorably; anything below 6% is simply overvalued. The market is pricing in flawless execution of the hypergrowth story for many years ahead, leaving zero margin of safety.

The cash flow picture is a serious structural red flag that goes beyond valuation. Net profit has grown impressively from INR 24 Cr to INR 110 Cr, but free cash flow has been negative in 3 of the last 4 years, summing to -367 Cr cumulatively. The company has funded this with debt (108 Cr → 482 Cr) and equity issuance, and cash has collapsed to near zero. Finance costs growing at 100% CAGR will increasingly erode earnings. For the Magic Formula to work, I need businesses that generate real cash — this one currently does not. At 39.5x earnings with no FCF, this is a speculative growth bet, not a value investment.
